style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: Psalm 51 is the prayer inside the storm of conviction; Psalm 32 is the testimony written on the far shore -- David's maskil, his teaching psalm, on what confession costs and what it buys. It opens with the double beatitude Paul quotes as the very definition of justification by faith: blessed the one whose rebellion is lifted off, whose sin is covered, to whom the LORD does not reckon iniquity (Romans 4:6-8). Then the clinical honesty of the silent months: bones wasting, groaning all day, God's hand heavy day and night, strength baked dry as a summer drought -- unconfessed sin as a physiology. The turn is one verse long: I acknowledged, I stopped covering, I said 'I will confess' -- and You forgave. Instantly. From that spring flows everything after: pray while He may be found and the floodwaters will not reach you; You are my hiding place, ringing me with songs of deliverance. Then God Himself takes the teacher's chair: I will instruct you with My eye upon you -- so do not be a mule that only moves by bit and bridle. The psalm ends where forgiveness always ends, in the loudest joy in the book: be glad, rejoice, shout, all you upright in heart.

1.text: Of David, a maskil. Oh the blessedness of the one whose rebellion is lifted away, whose sin is covered over!
1.amp: A Psalm of David, Maschil ['giving instruction', maskil, the KJV margin -- a teaching psalm]. Blessed [esher] is he whose transgression [pesha -- rebellion] is forgiven [nasa -- lifted off, carried away], whose sin [chataah] is covered [kasah].
1.notes: The forgiveness-verb is nasa (H5375), to lift and carry away -- the scapegoat's verb (cf. Leviticus 16:22): guilt picked up off the man and borne off. kasah (H3680), covered -- by God, which is the only covering that works; verse 5 will show what happens when the sinner tries the covering himself.

2.text: Oh the blessedness of the man to whom the LORD reckons no iniquity, and in whose spirit there is no deceit!
2.amp: Blessed [esher] is the man [adam] unto whom the LORD [YHWH] imputes [chashab -- reckons, credits] not iniquity [avon], and in whose spirit [ruach] there is no guile [remiyah -- deceit, self-deception].
2.notes: chashab (H2803) is bookkeeping language: the account where avon (H5771) is NOT entered. Paul takes these two verses as the Old Testament's clearest statement of righteousness credited apart from works (cf. Romans 4:6-8). The last clause is the entry condition: no remiyah (H7423) -- forgiveness comes to honesty, not to performance.

3.text: When I kept silent, my bones wore away through my groaning all day long.
3.amp: When I kept silence [charash], my bones [etsem] waxed old [balah -- wore out, wasted away] through my roaring [sheagah] all the day [yom] long.
3.notes: The paradox of the cover-up: charash (H2790), silent toward God, yet sheagah (H7581) -- the lion-roar of Psalm 22:1 -- all day inside. Sin unconfessed does not sit quietly; it grinds the etsem (H6106) like a millstone. David is describing the year between Bathsheba and Nathan (cf. 2 Samuel 12; Psalm 51).

4.text: For day and night Your hand pressed heavy upon me; my life's moisture was turned to the cracked dryness of high summer. Selah.
4.amp: For day [yomam] and night [layil] Your hand [yad] was heavy [kabad] upon me: my moisture [leshad -- sap, vital juice] is turned [haphak] into the drought [charabah -- the parched ground] of summer [qayits]. Selah [selah].
4.notes: kabad (H3513), the heaviness-word that elsewhere means glory: conviction as weight from the same hand. The body's leshad, its sap, haphak (H2015), inverted into charabah (H2725) -- August-dry ground where a life used to be. The heavy hand was mercy refusing to let the silence become comfortable.

5.text: Then I acknowledged my sin to You, and I stopped hiding my iniquity. I said, 'I will confess my rebellions to the LORD' -- and You Yourself forgave the guilt of my sin. Selah.
5.amp: I acknowledged [yada -- made known] my sin [chattath] unto You, and mine iniquity [avon] have I not hid [kasah]. I said [amar], 'I will confess [yadah] my transgressions [pesha] unto the LORD [YHWH]'; and You forgave [nasa -- lifted away] the iniquity [avon] of my sin. Selah.
5.notes: The hinge of the psalm, and the kasah-exchange at its center: David stops covering (kasah negated), and God does the covering of verse 1. All three sin-words of the opening return -- chattath, avon, pesha -- and the forgiveness lands before the confession is even finished: 'I said I WILL confess... and You forgave' (cf. Luke 15:20, the father running while the speech is half-rehearsed).

6.text: For this let everyone who is godly pray to You in the hour You may be found; surely when the great waters rise in flood, they will not reach him.
6.amp: For this shall every one that is godly [chasid -- covenant-faithful] pray [palal] unto You in a time ['of finding', matsa, the KJV margin] when You may be found: surely in the floods [sheteph] of great [rav] waters [mayim] they shall not come nigh [naga] unto him.
6.notes: David's private mercy becomes public doctrine: let every chasid (H2623) pray le-et metso, in the hour of finding (cf. Isaiah 55:6) -- forgiveness has business hours called 'now'. The sheteph (H7858), the flash-flood of judgment or trouble, rises to the confessed man's door and naga (H5060), touches him, not.

7.text: You are my hiding place; You keep guard over me in trouble; You surround me with ringing songs of deliverance. Selah.
7.amp: You are my hiding place [sether]; You shall preserve [natsar] me from trouble [tsar]; You shall compass [savav] me about with songs [ron -- ringing cries] of deliverance [palat]. Selah.
7.notes: sether (H5643), the hiding place of Psalm 91:1 -- and the marvel is WHO hides there: the man who spent verses 3-4 hiding FROM God now hides IN Him. The siege-verb savav (H5437) is turned to music: encircled not by enemies but by ron palat (H6405), deliverance-songs on every side.

8.text: 'I will give you insight and instruct you in the way you should go; I will counsel you with My eye upon you.'
8.amp: 'I will instruct [sakal -- give insight to] you and teach [yarah] you in the way [derek] which you shall go [yalak]: I will guide you with mine eye ['counsel thee, mine eye shall be upon thee', yaats, ayin, the KJV margin].'
8.notes: The Forgiver takes the teacher's chair -- the maskil inside the maskil. yarah (H3384) is the aiming-instruction of Psalm 25:8, and the method is intimacy itself: yaats (H3289) with the ayin (H5869) resting on you -- guidance by the look of a Father whose face you watch, not by the yank of a rope (which is exactly verse 9's warning).

9.text: Do not be like the horse or the mule, without understanding, whose tempers must be curbed with bit and bridle, or they will not come near you.
9.amp: Be ye not as the horse [sus], or as the mule [pered], which have no understanding [bin]: whose mouth must be held in [balam -- muzzled, restrained] with bit [metheg] and bridle [resen], lest they come not near [qarav] unto you.
9.notes: The alternative to eye-guidance: hardware. The sus and pered (H5483, H6505) move only under balam (H1102), external force -- and the point of the last clause is nearness: unrestrained, they will not qarav (H7126), come close. God prefers sons who read His eye to mules who fight His bit (cf. James 3:3, the same bit-image).

10.text: Many are the sorrows of the wicked, but covenant love surrounds the one who trusts in the LORD.
10.amp: Many [rav] sorrows [makob -- pains] shall be to the wicked [rasha]: but he that trusts [batach -- leans his weight] in the LORD [YHWH], mercy [chesed -- covenant love] shall compass [savav] him about.
10.notes: Two encirclements on offer: the rasha ringed by rav makob (H4341), pain upon pain -- the multiplied sorrows Psalm 16:4 priced for idolatry -- and the leaning man ringed by chesed (H2617). savav (H5437) a second time: everyone is surrounded by something; trust chooses the perimeter.

11.text: Be glad in the LORD and rejoice, you righteous ones, and shout for joy, all you upright in heart!
11.amp: Be glad [samach] in the LORD [YHWH], and rejoice [gil -- exult], ye righteous [tsaddiq]: and shout [ranan -- ring out] for joy, all ye that are upright [yashar] in heart [leb].
11.notes: Three joy-verbs in ascending volume -- samach, gil, ranan (H8055, H1523, H7442) -- assigned to the forgiven as a duty. The psalm that opened with lifted guilt closes with lifted voices: the tsaddiq here are verse 1-2's pardoned ones, righteous by the reckoning, and loud about it (cf. Romans 5:11).
